paper.title_en: Real Part Emergence in Purely Imaginary Quasinormal Modes in Perturbed de Sitter Braneworlds
paper.abstract_en: For braneworlds with infinite extra dimensions, an analysis of the stability of the characteristic spectrum is essential for understanding their dynamical properties; in this study, we investigate the stability of the gravitational quasinormal-mode (QNM) spectrum of a thick de Sitter braneworld with a noncompact extra dimension, where the unperturbed background supports a localized graviton zero mode and a tower of purely imaginary QNMs. We first reconstruct the response of the warp factor and tensor effective potential to a smooth double-kink deformation of the bulk scalar field, and then introduce a superpotential deformation that parametrizes the resulting double-barrier structure; the deformed frequency-domain spectrum develops QNM pairs with nonzero real parts, and for the representative family studied here, a weak deformation can already generate a complex branch, although the least-damped pole remains purely imaginary in part of the parameter range. In the time domain, the QNM-dominated channel exhibits a transient damped oscillatory stage, whereas the original-potential evolution becomes dominated by the zero-mode sector at late times over the simulated interval. These results identify the double-barrier geometry as the model-specific realization of a more general sensitivity of outgoing, non-self-adjoint spectra, establish a robust model-level mechanism for oscillatory QNM imprints, and provide a dimensionless benchmark for future source-to-detector analyses, while quantitative detector detectability and cosmological-parameter inference require source, response, and noise modeling beyond the present analysis.
